title: Uniform circular motion and centripetal force

step.script: In uniform circular motion, an object follows a circle at constant speed. Its distance from the center stays equal to the radius.

primitives.meaning: circular path of the moving object

step.script: Velocity points tangent to the circle. Although speed stays constant, velocity changes direction, so the object accelerates toward the center.
Newton's second law requires a net inward force. Centripetal describes its direction, not a new force: tension, gravity, or friction can supply it.

ops.content: Double speed → four times the force

checkpoint.question: At the same mass and radius, how does the required inward force change when speed doubles?
checkpoint.expected_gist: It quadruples because centripetal force is proportional to speed squared.
